newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia's fund conference set for April-World Bank.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia's fund conference set for April-World Bank.

text.p: An international donors' conference for Bosnia has been postponed at least until April because the country's inter-ethnic government has yet to adopt an economic reform package, the World Bank said on Monday.

"I don't think if we organised the donors' conference in March many donors would come, so we really expect and hope that by mid-April things will be back on track," Rory O'Sullivan, head of the World Bank's Sarajevo office, told Reuters.

The conference, which aims to raise $1.4 billion in reconstruction funds for 1997, was originally set for March. But donors first want Bosnia to adopt economic reforms needed to clinch an agreement with the International Monetary Fund.

The package includes a law on a single central bank, state budgets, servicing of external debt and a tariff law. Diplomats say the main stumbling block among Bosnia's political leaders is the proposed central bank law.
Michael Steiner, deputy to the international High Representative to Bosnia, recently blamed authorities from Bosnia's Serb entity for obstructing passage of the central law.
"It's clearly representatives from one entity blocking the adoption of the necessary laws. Nobody should think that he can hold another entity hostage," Steiner said in a radio interview this month.
If agreed, the central bank would be the sole authority for issuing a single currency for the country's Serb and Moslem-Croat territories.

Serb nationalist leaders opposed to a unitary Bosnian state are reluctant to accept a single central bank. In the Bosnian Serb entity, banks currently use the Yugoslav dinar from neighbouring Yugoslavia.
Steiner and other Western envoys say donors are no longer interested in emergency relief aid and want to see economic reforms before committing funds.
"Otherwise, the money would be thrown out the window if you don't have the right economic network," Steiner said.
